new: By doing so, that is, by remembering the knowers of the Veda's meaning, all the deities presiding over the Veda dwell in his heart; and one who remembers and reveres them thereby pleases those deities.
basis: Kannada p.525: ಸಮಸ್ತ ವೇದಾಭಿಮಾನಿದೇವತೆಗಳು ಈತನ ಹೃದಯದಲ್ಲಿಯೇ ವಾಸಿಸುವರು. ಇವರನ್ನು ಸ್ಮರಣಮಾಡಿ ನಮಸ್ಕಾರಮಾಡುವವನು ಈ ದೇವತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಸಂತೋಷಪಡಿಸಿದಂತಾಗುವುದು

old: receives none of that honour. He gains no distinction whatsoever. Where dry firewood is heaped upon a fire, does it not burn? It does — and correspondingly, a reciter who merely recites is like Vedic speech with no ability to ignite; only one who recites *with understanding* generates real fruit.
new: receives less honour than the one who knows the meaning. Reciting the Vedic text taught by the guru, without knowing its meaning, gives the reciter no knowledge of the Veda's meaning and inspires him in nothing. Does firewood thrown where there is no fire burn, however dry it is? Likewise the words a reciter utters, though they are Vedic words, carry little weight; only if he utters them knowing their meaning does great fruit arise.
basis: Kannada p.526: ಬೆಂಕಿಯಿಲ್ಲದ ಕಡೆ ಎಸೆದ ಸೌದೆಯು ಎಷ್ಟು ಒಣಗಿದ್ದರೂ ಉರಿಯುವುದೇ?; the knower gets more honour than the reciter (not 'none'); English had the fire present

old: Here the agent-word governing the action is grammatically ambiguous — there's no grammatical doubt as such, but on a purely grammar-based reading,

old: Should we not simply praise it and undertake it? Is it right to expound its meaning through elaborate labor? Must one understand the Veda's meaning? To all this we answer: we have great reverence for meaning-knowledge, and no contempt whatsoever.
new: Why do you expound its praise and its meaning with so much labour? Would it not be enough simply to say that the Veda's meaning should be known? To this we must reply: we have faith in meaning-knowledge, but why do you hate it so?
basis: Kannada p.539: ಅರ್ಥಜ್ಞಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಮಗೇಕೆ ಇಷ್ಟು ಭಕ್ತಿ? ... ನಾವೇನೋ ಅರ್ಥಜ್ಞಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಶ್ರದ್ಧೆಯನ್ನಿಟ್ಟಿದ್ದೇವೆ. ಆದರೆ ನಿಮಗೇಕೆ ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಅಷ್ಟು ದ್ವೇಷ?

old: Even though the words of very profound texts may, in some places, be difficult to grasp, their deep meaning is still understood by those who study, and because of this — the Angas being the means to that understanding — the wise call the Veda's own meaning "aparā" (lower). Those learned in the tradition of Shiksha and the other Angas state, on the authority of the very text quoted above—
new: Because the Veda is extremely profound — its words intricately joined and its meaning deep and hidden, hard to grasp — the six Angas beginning with Shiksha have arisen to make its meaning rightly known. For this very reason those who know the Atharvaveda, in the Mundaka Upanishad, call the Vedas with the six Angas the "lower knowledge" (aparā vidyā)—
basis: Kannada p.547: ಅತಿಗಂಭೀರವಾದ ... ವೇದಾರ್ಥವನ್ನು ಸರಿಯಾಗಿ ತಿಳಿಯಿಸುವುದಕ್ಕೆಂದು ಶಿಕ್ಷಾ ಮೊದಲಾದ ಷಡಂಗಗಳು ಹೊರಟಿವೆ. ಆದುದರಿಂದಲೇ ಅಥರ್ವಣವೇದವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿದವರು ಮುಂಡಕೋಪನಿಷತ್ತಿನಲ್ಲಿ ... ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯೆಯೆಂದು ಹೇಳುವರು

old: Because this cannot be beginningless, and because it is a mere instrument for grasping the meaning of the Veda's Brahmana portion — which itself expounds dharma — it is spoken of as the "lower" knowledge.
new: The knowledge that makes known the imperishable, beginningless Parabrahman is called parā. The Vedas with the six Angas teach the karma-kanda and are the cause of the means to dharma-knowledge; therefore the name aparā suits them.
basis: Kannada p.547: ನಾಶರಹಿತವೂ ಅನಾದಿಯೂ ಆದ ಪರಬ್ರಹ್ಮಸ್ವರೂಪವನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸುವ ವಿದ್ಯೆಯೇ ಪರಾವಿದ್ಯೆ. ಷಡಂಗಸಹಿತವಾದ ವೇದಗಳು ಕರ್ಮಕಾಂಡವನ್ನು ಬೋಧಿಸಿ ... ಅಪರಾವಿದ್ಯೆಯೆಂಬ ಹೆಸರು ಸಲ್ಲುವುದು

old: Those wishing to know these Vedic matters should study Śikṣā first among the Angas — for those who begin here find it easier to work through the meanings arranged in other treatises. **We shall therefore first look briefly at the subjects treated in this Anga before proceeding to the other Angas.**
new: As said before, knowledge of the six Angas beginning with Śikṣā is necessary for understanding the Veda's meaning. **We now examine closely the subjects treated in Śikṣā and the other Anga-works; whoever wishes to know more should consult the original works such as the Pāṇinīya-śikṣā.**

new: there is a separate Śikṣā work for each Veda, and many authors have written many kinds of Śikṣā-works for each Veda; they are known by the names of their authors: Pāṇinīya-śikṣā, Nāradīya-śikṣā, Bhāradvāja-śikṣā and so on.
